questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman in a burn unit develops septicemia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The isolate produces exotoxin A, a toxin present in most clinical isolates of this organism. Which of the following best describes how this toxin kills host cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It blocks elongation factor 2, halting host protein synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cleaves ribosomal RNA within the 60S ribosomal subunit

choices.label: C
choices.text: It degrades membrane phospholipids and lyses the cell

choices.label: D
choices.text: It prevents the release of the inhibitory neurotransmitters

choices.label: E
choices.text: It raises intracellular cAMP by modifying a G protein

explanation.summary: Pseudomonas exotoxin A blocks elongation factor 2, shutting down protein synthesis and killing the target cell.
explanation.whyCorrect: Strains of Pseudomonas secrete several toxins that damage host cells, and exotoxin A is present in most clinical isolates. It blocks elongation factor 2 activity, which is critical for translation. Without functioning EF-2 the cell cannot make protein and ultimately dies.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Inactivation of the 60S ribosomal subunit is the mechanism of Shiga toxin, not exotoxin A.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Phospholipase activity that lyses membranes describes the alpha toxin of Clostridium perfringens in gas gangrene.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blocking release of GABA and glycine describes tetanospasmin from Clostridium tetani.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Raising cAMP by modifying a G protein describes toxins such as cholera toxin, heat-labile toxin of ETEC, anthrax toxin, and pertussis toxin.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A wound isolate of Pseudomonas aeruginosa produces a blue pigment that is directly toxic to host cells, including leukocytes and epithelial cells. Which of the following is this pigment?

explanation.summary: Pyocyanin is the blue Pseudomonas pigment that is toxic to leukocytes and epithelial cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: P. aeruginosa makes two pigments, pyocyanin and pyoverdine. Pyocyanin is blue and toxic for cells, including leukocytes and epithelial cells, so it contributes directly to tissue damage. Together with pyoverdine it gives colonies their blue-to-aqua appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alginate is the polysaccharide of the mucoid capsule; it is not a pigment and is not cytotoxic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Exotoxin A is a secreted protein toxin, not a pigment, and it acts by blocking elongation factor 2.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipopolysaccharide is the gram-negative outer membrane endotoxin and does not color the colony.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyoverdine is the other Pseudomonas pigment, but it is yellow and fluorescent and functions in iron binding.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A flask of Pseudomonas culture glows yellow-green when a ultraviolet lamp is shone on it in a darkened laboratory. The molecule responsible also binds iron for the bacterium. Which of the following is it?

explanation.summary: Pyoverdine is a yellow, fluorescent, iron-binding pigment that makes Pseudomonas fluoresce under UV light.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pyoverdine is one of the two pigments produced by P. aeruginosa. It is yellow and fluorescent, and it binds iron. Other Pseudomonas species can produce pyoverdine as well, which is why they fluoresce under ultraviolet light.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alginate forms the mucoid capsule seen in cystic fibrosis isolates and does not fluoresce.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Exotoxin A is a secreted protein toxin that blocks elongation factor 2 and has no pigment function.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The polysaccharide capsule contributes to adherence and protection, not to fluorescence or iron acquisition.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyocyanin is blue and cytotoxic; it is not the fluorescent iron-binding pigment.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Sputum from an intubated patient grows a motile gram-negative rod that does not ferment lactose and is oxidase positive. The colonies are blue-green. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

explanation.summary: A motile, non-lactose-fermenting, oxidase-positive gram-negative rod with blue-green colonies is Pseudomonas.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudomonas species are gram-negative, do not ferment lactose, and are oxidase positive. They are motile by a single polar flagellum, and pyocyanin and pyoverdine give the colonies an aqua or green color. This combination identifies the organism in the laboratory.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acinetobacter is a non-motile, oxidase-negative coccobacillus with colorless or creamy colonies.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Escherichia coli also ferments lactose, which separates it from Pseudomonas on MacConkey agar.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Klebsiella pneumoniae ferments lactose and does not produce a blue-green pigment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Salmonella does not ferment lactose but is oxidase negative and produces no pigment.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Two gram-negative rods from different patients both fail to ferment lactose on MacConkey agar; one is later identified as Pseudomonas and the other as a Salmonella species. Which of the following laboratory findings best separates Pseudomonas from non-lactose-fermenting organisms such as Salmonella and Shigella?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ability to grow on standard blood agar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram stain morphology of the organism

explanation.summary: Oxidase positivity distinguishes Pseudomonas from the other non-lactose-fermenting gram-negative rods.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two tests anchor the identification of Pseudomonas. The inability to ferment lactose separates it from lactose fermenters such as E. coli and Klebsiella. Oxidase production then separates it from the non-lactose-fermenting gram-negatives such as Salmonella and Shigella, which are oxidase negative.

whyWrongByChoice.A: All of these organisms grow readily on routine laboratory media.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Catalase is not the test used to distinguish these gram-negative rods from one another.
whyWrongByChoice.C: All are gram-negative rods on Gram stain, so morphology does not separate them.
whyWrongByChoice.D: All three organisms in question fail to ferment lactose, so this test cannot tell them apart.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Sputum from a 17-year-old with cystic fibrosis grows Pseudomonas colonies that are strikingly slimy and wet in appearance, unlike the dry colonies grown from a burn wound isolate on the adjacent plate. Overproduction of which of the following explains this mucoid phenotype?

explanation.summary: The mucoid capsule of Pseudomonas is made of alginate and is characteristic of cystic fibrosis isolates.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudomonas can produce a mucoid capsule made of alginate, a polysaccharide that absorbs a large multiple of its own weight in water. Strains expressing this capsule adhere to and colonize mucus far better. Mucoid strains are almost exclusively isolated from the lungs of cystic fibrosis patients.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Exotoxin A is a secreted toxin; in chronically colonized CF lungs these toxins are actually downregulated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipopolysaccharide is present on all gram-negative bacteria and does not confer the mucoid appearance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyocyanin is the blue cytotoxic pigment and affects colony color rather than texture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyoverdine is a fluorescent iron-binding pigment and does not create a slimy colony.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: The mucoid capsule that Pseudomonas expresses in the cystic fibrosis lung is a polysaccharide with a striking capacity to hold water, which helps the organism adhere to and colonize airway mucus. Approximately how much water can it absorb relative to its own weight?

explanation.summary: Alginate can absorb roughly 200-300 times its own weight in water.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alginate is the polysaccharide of the Pseudomonas mucoid capsule and absorbs about 200-300 times its weight in water. That water-holding capacity is what makes the colonies visibly slimy and lets the organism bind and colonize the thick mucus of the cystic fibrosis airway.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This underestimates the capacity by roughly two orders of magnitude.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is far below the figure described for alginate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is still well short of the actual water-binding capacity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This overstates the capacity by about tenfold.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Pseudomonas isolates recovered from the chronically colonized lungs of cystic fibrosis patients express far fewer secreted toxins than isolates recovered from acute wound infections in other patients. Which of the following best explains this behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibiotic exposure selects for strains unable to produce toxins

choices.label: B
choices.text: Host mucus chemically inactivates the secreted bacterial toxins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of the polar flagellum prevents export of secreted toxins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Toxin genes are transferred away to other bacteria in the biofilm

choices.label: E
choices.text: White blood cells penetrate mucus poorly, so toxins are dispensable

explanation.summary: In the cystic fibrosis lung Pseudomonas downregulates most virulence factors because white blood cells cannot reach it through the mucus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudomonas colonizing cystic fibrosis mucus stops producing most of its virulence factors. White blood cells cannot infiltrate the mucus layer well, so the organism can save energy by shutting those factors off. Virulence factor reduction of this kind is uncommon among pathogenic bacteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotics select for resistance, not for loss of toxin production.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The toxins are not being made in the first place; this is a change in bacterial gene expression, not chemical inactivation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flagellar loss relates to motility, and toxin secretion does not depend on the flagellum here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gene transfer within a biofilm does not explain the coordinated downregulation seen in these isolates.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A 26-year-old with cystic fibrosis has had recurrent pulmonary infections and a steady decline in lung function since childhood. Which of the following is the most common cause of death in patients with this disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hepatic cirrhosis from biliary tract obstruction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Respiratory failure from chronic lung infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Septicemia arising from urinary tract infection

explanation.summary: Respiratory failure due to chronic infection is the most common cause of death in cystic fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thick mucus lets bacteria colonize deeper in the lungs and in higher numbers, which drives chronic inflammation. That inflammation progressively destroys the lungs and increases the risk of further infection, a cycle in which Pseudomonas plays a central role. Respiratory failure from these chronic infections is the most common cause of death.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Liver disease can complicate cystic fibrosis but does not account for most deaths.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intestinal obstruction occurs in cystic fibrosis but is not the leading cause of mortality.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pancreatic involvement causes malabsorption and is managed with enzyme replacement; it is not the usual cause of death.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinary tract infection is not a characteristic complication of cystic fibrosis.
